title: Uniqueness of the pinched-cube cosimplicial augmentation
statement: Use simplicial sets, ordinary nerves and standard simplices from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $Q^\bullet$ be the cosimplicial pinched cubes of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]: $Q^n$ is the quotient of the nerve of nonempty subsets of $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ which, on the subcube where coordinate $i$ is $1$, identifies simplices having the same coordinates strictly greater than $i$. Monotone maps act by direct image of subsets. Let $\mu_n:Q^n\to\Delta^n$ be the descended maximum-of-subsets map. A cosimplicial map means a family of simplicial maps $b_n:Q^n\to\Delta^n$ satisfying $b_mQ(\theta)=\Delta(\theta)b_n$ for every weakly increasing $\theta:[n]\to[m]$. Every cosimplicial map $b_\bullet$ equals $\mu_\bullet$.

source.place: Agent lemma for the point normalization in Section 3.2.1 (Proposition 3.2.1.14), using the pinched-cube quotient of lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching; extracted from the inherited comparison proof step 4. WANTED: local HTT archive.

proof.text: Write $q_n:N(P_n)\to Q^n$ for the quotient map in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], and write $[I]$ for the vertex represented by a nonempty subset $I\subseteq[n]$. Put $k=\max I$. In the relation subcube with coordinate $k$ equal to $1$, the vertices $I$ and $\{k\}$ have identical (empty) coordinates strictly greater than $k$; hence $[I]=[\{k\}]$. Thus every vertex has a singleton representative. Moreover $Q^0$ has exactly one simplex in every degree, since $P_0=\{\{0\}\}$ and taking its quotient makes no change. These are direct uses of the stated degreewise quotient and nerve definitions.

source.place: Section 2.2.2, cubical quotient and maximum augmentation immediately before Proposition 2.2.2.7, printed p.76; agent-written uniqueness argument for the normalization used in Proposition 3.2.1.14, printed p.177.

proof.text: Let $b_\bullet$ be a cosimplicial map as in the statement. For $k\in[n]$ let $\iota_k:[0]\to[n]$ have value $k$. By the direct-image action in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], $Q(\iota_k)$ sends the sole vertex $v$ of $Q^0$ to $[\{k\}]$. The sole vertex of $\Delta^0$ is $0$, so $b_0(v)=0$. Cosimplicial naturality therefore gives $b_n([\{k\}])=\Delta(\iota_k)(b_0(v))=k$. Step 1 now gives $b_n([I])=\max I$ for every nonempty $I$. This calculation includes $n=0$ and both endpoint vertices.

source.place: Section 2.2.2, cubical quotient and maximum augmentation immediately before Proposition 2.2.2.7, printed p.76; agent-written uniqueness argument for the normalization used in Proposition 3.2.1.14, printed p.177.

proof.text: Fix $n,r\geq0$ and an $r$-simplex $z$ of $Q^n$. The degreewise quotient supplies a representative chain $I_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq I_r$ of nonempty subsets. Its $j$th vertex is $[I_j]$: in the nerve, restriction along $[0]\to[r]$ with value $j$ selects $I_j$, and the quotient map is simplicial. Since $b_n$ is simplicial, Step 2 says the $j$th vertex of $b_n(z)$ is $\max I_j$. By the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $r$-simplex of $\Delta^n$ is a weakly increasing function $[r]\to[n]$ and its $j$th vertex is its value at $j$. Thus $b_n(z)$ is exactly $j\mapsto\max I_j$. The descended nerve-of-maximum map $\mu_n$ in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] has this same value on the representative chain. Hence $b_n(z)=\mu_n(z)$. Equality for every $r,z$ and then every $n$ proves $b_\bullet=\mu_\bullet$.
